intro: Kwan Phayao is the largest freshwater lake in northern Thailand, so eating fish is just a normal part of life here — tilapia, redtail catfish, snakehead, and clown knifefish all pulled straight from the lake. Plenty of lakeside spots grill, fry, and tom-yum the catch fresh while you watch the sun go down over the water. We have picked the places that are genuinely open and that locals in Phayao actually eat at.

blocks.html: Coming to Phayao without eating fish by the lake is like not really arriving — the fish here is properly local. Kwan Phayao holds several kinds of freshwater fish that fishermen haul in and sell to the lakeside restaurants from early morning, so the flesh is fresh and firm, with none of that muddy taste people often worry about. Most places can grill, fry, steam, or tom-yum it, so you can order it however you like.
Before you order, knowing a little about the lake's fish makes the whole thing more fun. Each kind suits a different way of cooking.

items: Tilapia (pla nin) — the lake's most popular fish. Firm flesh, great salt-grilled or fried with fish sauce, and the easiest one to start with if you are new to it.
Redtail catfish (pla khang) — a soft-fleshed catfish with just the right richness, best known in tom yum and sour curry. A touch pricier than tilapia but worth it.
Snakehead (pla chon) — sweet, firm flesh that works fried, in tom yum, or steamed with lime. A fish northern Thais eat often.
Clown knifefish (pla krai) — chewy, springy flesh, usually made into fish cakes or blanched with a dipping sauce. Harder to find than the others.
Butter catfish (pla nuea on) — thin, soft flesh that melts in your mouth; fried with garlic it comes out crisp outside and tender inside. A dish many places take pride in.

blocks.text: Lakeside fish spots locals actually go to

blocks.html: These are the fish houses and lakeside restaurants with standout fish menus, ordered by how strong the fish is and the riverside atmosphere. Prices are rough ranges — fresh fish is charged by weight, and you can pick yours from the tank out front.

items.name: Nong Ang
items.blurb: A fish house by the Kwan Phayao pier known above all for its grilled fish, with live fish to choose from out front — redtail catfish, tilapia, clown knifefish, fish roe, and fermented fish (pla som). You sit right by the water with a cool breeze, and it is the spot most people think of before any other.
items.meta: By Kwan Phayao pier · grilled fish / pla som · about 250–500 THB per person

items.name: Aurora Kitchen
items.blurb: A lakeside spot with a wide-open view of the water on all sides, focused on fish and pesticide-free vegetables they grow themselves. The standouts are garlic-fried butter catfish and grilled tilapia miang wraps, and the tom yum redtail catfish is done well too. A good place to settle in for the sunset.
items.meta: Lakeside · fried fish / grilled-fish miang · tom yum redtail catfish around 239 THB

items.name: Chitlom Chom Kwan
items.blurb: A lakeside restaurant serving Thai, northern, and Isan food. The fish dish not to miss is the punchy tom yum redtail catfish, great alongside duck larb and gaeng hangle. The view is lovely and you can linger for hours — it stays open late.
items.meta: 684/5 Wiang subdistrict · open 10:00–23:00 · tom yum redtail catfish

items.name: So Good Phayao
items.blurb: A roomy lakeside spot with a waterfront zone lined with coconut palms and live music in the evenings. The fish to order is tilapia fried with fish sauce and garlic-fried fish, paired with sour curry of cha-om omelet and shrimp, and tom yum redtail catfish.
items.meta: 222 Moo 17, Ban Tom subdistrict · open 10:00–00:00 · live music

items.name: Khao Tom Pho Thong
items.blurb: A spot near Kwan Phayao known for its house-recipe tom yum snakehead — deep, well-rounded flavor with fresh, firm snakehead. A good choice for a simple but satisfying dinner.
items.meta: Kwan Phayao area · tom yum snakehead · easy on the wallet

items.name: Tha Ruea Boran, Thung Kio
items.blurb: A fish-eating spot on the lake's Thung Kio side, right by the water with a strong breeze and cool air. There are live shrimp and fresh fish to pick from — a good place to sit in the evening and catch the lake wind.
items.meta: Thung Kio side · fresh fish / fresh shrimp · seating right by the water

items.name: Niyom Suk Kwan Phayao
items.blurb: A lakeside restaurant that locals have eaten at for years. Made-to-order dishes and fish done several ways — fried, steamed, tom yum — at friendly prices. A solid pick for a family meal.
items.meta: Lakeside, Kwan Phayao · steamed fish / fried fish · friendly prices

items.name: Kinpla Phayao
items.blurb: A place built around fish, just as the name says (kinpla means 'eat fish'). It does grilled fish, fried fish, and a fiery tom yum, set on Phahonyothin Road close to town and open straight through from midday into the evening.
items.meta: Phahonyothin Rd, Wiang subdistrict · open 11:00–21:00 · fish-focused menu

blocks.title: Ordering fish for value
blocks.html: Fresh fish is charged by weight, so if there are two or three of you, a medium tilapia or snakehead is a better bet than a big one you cannot finish. Want to try more than one flavor? Many places are happy to do half grilled and half tom yum.

blocks.text: Fish dishes to try at least once

blocks.html: If you are not sure where to begin, these three are the basics that most lakeside spots do well — and a good gauge of how skilled a place is.

items.name: Salt-grilled tilapia
items.blurb: Packed in salt and grilled until the skin is taut and the flesh inside stays soft and juicy. Eat it with seafood dipping sauce and fresh herbs — this is the dish where you taste the lake most clearly.

items.name: Tom yum redtail catfish
items.blurb: A rich-fleshed catfish in a thick, punchy tom yum — sour, spicy, and well-balanced. Slurping it hot in the evening by the water is the high point of the meal.

items.name: Garlic-fried butter catfish
items.blurb: Thin flesh fried until crisp outside and tender inside, scattered with fragrant fried garlic. Kids will eat it; adults get hooked.

blocks.html: Lakeside fish spots are most fun in the evening, when you can eat as the sun sets behind the lake and the breeze off the water cools things down. Aim to arrive around 4 pm to grab a waterfront table before they fill up. Fresh fish tends to be most plentiful from morning to early afternoon, so if you want a nice-looking one, getting there before dusk gives you more to choose from.

blocks.title: Worth being straight about
blocks.html: Lakeside spots get very busy on holidays and waterfront tables go fast, so if you are coming on a Saturday or Sunday, call to book or arrive early. Some fish, like clown knifefish, can sell out quickly because supply is limited — not every place has every kind every day.

faq.q: Which fish restaurant by Kwan Phayao is good?
faq.a: Nong Ang is known for grilled fish and has live fish to pick from out front. Aurora Kitchen and So Good Phayao stand out for their lakeside views and fried fish. If you love tom yum fish, Chitlom Chom Kwan and Khao Tom Pho Thong do it well. Choose based on which dishes you want and the kind of atmosphere you are after.

faq.q: Does Kwan Phayao fish taste muddy?
faq.a: Most lakeside spots catch the fish fresh and cook it right away, so the flesh is fresh and rarely tastes muddy — especially tilapia and redtail catfish, which are popular grilled and in tom yum. If you are worried about the taste, salt-grilling or a punchy tom yum covers it well.

faq.q: What kinds of fish are in Kwan Phayao?
faq.a: The popular ones are tilapia, redtail catfish, snakehead, clown knifefish, and butter catfish. Tilapia is good grilled or fried, redtail catfish shines in tom yum and sour curry, snakehead works both fried and in tom yum, while clown knifefish and butter catfish are harder to find and often sell out fast.

faq.q: How much does eating fish by Kwan Phayao cost?
faq.a: Fresh fish is charged by the weight of each fish. A fish meal for two or three comes to roughly 250–500 THB per person depending on the type and how many dishes you order. Tilapia is the most affordable; redtail catfish and butter catfish run a little higher. A plate of tom yum redtail catfish is around 200 THB and up.

faq.q: When should I go to the lakeside fish restaurants?
faq.a: The evening before sunset is best — you get both the cool breeze and the lake view. Aim to arrive around 4 pm to grab a waterfront table. On busy holidays, call ahead to book. Fresh fish is most plentiful from morning to early afternoon.
